samples.summary: New slide text-body walk accepts a text body with `blocks` absent, which is a TypeError in every renderer of the stored deck
samples.evidence: `assertValidTextBodyBlocks` early-returns when `blocks === undefined || blocks === null` (line 671), so `PUT` bodies like `{id:'e1',type:'text',frame:{},data:{}}` or `{type:'shape',data:{text:{}}}` pass validation and are persisted verbatim by `writeSlidesRoot`. On read, `isTextBodyEmpty(body)` → `isBlocksEmpty(body.blocks)` does `blocks.length === 0` (packages/slides/src/model/element.ts:653) and `migrateElement` (packages/slides/src/model/migrate.ts:155) does NOT backfill `data.blocks` — only shape fill/stroke are migrated. So `blocks` undefined throws `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'length')` for every viewer of the deck. This is exactly the failure mode `normalizeSlideInlines` was added to prevent for `inlines`; the same repair (`body.blocks = []`) is not applied here.

samples.summary: Slide block with no `style` is accepted, but the PPTX exporter dereferences `block.style` unconditionally
samples.evidence: `assertValidSlideBlocks` only validates `style` when it is present (`if (block.style !== undefined && block.style !== null)`, line 694) — deliberately, per the doc comment. But `packages/slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts:99` does `ALGN.get(block.style.alignment)` and lines 105/107/113/119/122 read `block.style.marginLeft/textIndent/lineHeight/marginTop/marginBottom` with no guard, so a stored block without `style` throws during PPTX export of that deck. The canvas path survives only because `text-renderer.ts` normalizes styles first; the export path does not. Same class as the `inlines` repair — either repair `block.style = {}` or reject.

samples.summary: `typeof block.style !== 'object'` accepts an array as a block style
samples.evidence: Line 695 (`if (typeof block.style !== 'object')`) and the docs-arm equivalent at line 371 (`!b.style || typeof b.style !== 'object'`) both let `style: []` through, since `typeof [] === 'object'`. It is then handed to `assertValidBlockStyle` where every field reads `undefined`, so the payload is stored as an array where a `BlockStyle` object is expected. Harmless for the current spread-based readers but the check does not mean what it says; `Array.isArray` should be excluded.

samples.summary: GET → PUT round-trip 400s for a docs table cell that has no block children (reader emits `id: ''`, validator requires a non-empty id)
samples.evidence: `treeNodeToCell` synthesizes a fallback block with `id: ''` when a cell node has zero `block` children (docs-tree.ts:329). `assertValidBlock` rejects `id` that is not a non-empty string (docs-content.controller.ts:365), and this diff extends that same walker to header/footer and re-affirms round-trip identity as a design goal. A document containing such a cell therefore cannot be re-PUT unchanged. The id check itself pre-dates this change, so confidence that it is reachable in practice is low (it requires a cell node with no block children in the CRDT).

samples.summary: The new `type !== 'table'` guard protects table→X but not X←table: converting an existing table block to a non-table type still splices an inline in front of its row nodes
samples.evidence: Line 1469 guards on the *target* type. Converting an existing table block to e.g. `paragraph` takes the else-branch (target is not 'table', and a table block's `block.inlines` is always `[]`), so `editByPath([...blockPath,0],[...blockPath,0], buildInlineNode(...))` inserts a text node ahead of row 0 — the exact shape the comment says must never happen — leaving stale `row` children under a `paragraph` node. The reader filters children by type so the rows become invisible rather than corrupting other paths, and reaching this needs `setBlockType` on a table block itself (the caret normally sits in a cell block), hence low confidence on reachability.

samples.summary: Inline-style clearing still uses the subtree-spanning `removeStyleByPath` the new `removeNodeStyle` was introduced to replace
samples.evidence: `applyStyle` at line 1918 keeps `tree.removeStyleByPath([...blockPath, i], [...blockPath, i + 1], removeAttrs)`, the pattern `removeNodeStyle`'s doc comment (line 258-272) calls out as subtree-wide rather than node-scoped. It is harmless today because an inline node's only children are text nodes (which carry no attributes), but the two paths now disagree on the stated invariant.

verdict.reason: The described code is present and behaves as claimed: assertValidTextBodyBlocks early-returns on absent/null `blocks` (docs-content.controller.ts:670-671), so payloads like `{type:'shape',data:{text:{}}}` or a text element with `data:{}` pass validation (reached via lines 618-624, 650) and are stored verbatim by writeSlidesRoot (slides-tree.ts:97-110, no normalization). No reader repairs it: migrate.ts:155-168 only migrates shape fill/stroke, and isBlocksEmpty dereferences `blocks.length` (element.ts:651-656) via isTextBodyEmpty (text-renderer.ts:165-167). The frontend Yorkie read repairs only TEXT elements (yorkie-slides-store.ts:495 `?? []`); shape and table element data go through the generic unwrap (yorkie-slides-store.ts:569-575) untouched, so paintShapeText — whose only guard is `if (!data.text) return;` and `{}` is truthy (shape-renderer.ts:445-449) — and table-renderer.ts:229 hit `undefined.length` and throw in the canvas render loop for every viewer of the deck. That is a real, reachable crash/data-persistence defect in the correctness lane; only the finding's "every renderer" wording is mildly over-broad, which does not refute it.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. packages/slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts:99 does `ALGN.get(block.style.alignment)` and :105/:107/:112/:119/:122 read block.style.* with no guard, reached for every block via textBodyToXml (:34-36) from shape.ts:203/:247, slide.ts:207 and table.ts:104 — all of which pass model blocks through verbatim. The only normalizeBlockStyle call in packages/slides is view/canvas/text-renderer.ts:263 (canvas only); exportPptx (export/pptx/index.ts:130-167) does no block normalization. Neither the frontend store (yorkie-slides-store.ts:495-510) nor the backend serializer (yorkie/slides-tree.ts:52-110) backfills style on read/write. Meanwhile the PUT validator at docs-content.controller.ts:694 only validates style when present, and its repair helper normalizeSlideInlines (:752-788) fills only inlines and inline.style, never block.style (contrast the docs arm at :371-373 which requires style). So a deck persisted with a style-less slide block throws a TypeError during PPTX export — a missing-guard crash on a real path, in the correctness lane. No counterexample found in the exporter, store, serializer, CLI or frontend export chain.

finding.summary: setBlockType on a table block inserts a stray inline node as the table node's first child, shifting every row index — the new test exercises exactly this call and only passes because the reader filters children by type 'row'
finding.evidence: The delta adds `store.setBlockType(tableBlock.id, 'table')` (packages/frontend/tests/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.test.ts, 'should not strip list/heading attrs from blocks nested in its cells'). In setBlockType, after the styleByPath/removeNodeStyle writes, the `else if (block.inlines.length === 0)` branch at yorkie-doc-store.ts:1469 runs for any non-HR/page-break type; a table block always has `inlines: []` (treeNodeToBlock:443), so `tree.editByPath([...blockPath,0],[...blockPath,0], buildInlineNode({text:'',style:{}}))` inserts an `inline` element as child 0 of the TABLE node. Nothing filters that out on write. Read-back hides it (treeNodeToBlock:432 keeps only `c.type === 'row'`), so the new assertions pass — but the CRDT tree now has rows at child indices 1..n while `findBlockInTable`/`resolveBlockTreePath` (lines 791-813, 820) address a cell block as `[...tablePath, rowIdx, cellIdx, blockIdx]`, i.e. row r at child index r. Any subsequent edit to a cell of that table therefore targets the wrong tree node (off by one) or the stray inline. The guard `if (type === 'horizontal-rule' || type === 'page-break')` should also exclude `type === 'table'` (and any block carrying tableData).

verdict.reason: The quoted condition does not exist in the repository. yorkie-doc-store.ts:1469 is `} else if (type !== 'table' && block.inlines.length === 0) {` — the `type === 'table'` exclusion the finding asks to add is already there, with a comment at :1470-1473 stating exactly the row-index-shift rationale. The cache-side twin at :1494 carries the same `type !== 'table'` guard, so neither the CRDT tree nor the cached Block gets a stray inline. The finding's claim that the new test "only passes because the reader filters children by type 'row'" is also wrong: tests/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:2005-2007 reads the raw tree via `doc.getRoot().content.getRootTreeNode().children[0]` and asserts `children.map(c => c.type)` equals `['row']`, deliberately bypassing the `filter(c => c.type === 'row')` reader at yorkie-doc-store.ts:432-434. With no inline inserted, the off-by-one against findBlockInTable/resolveBlockTreePath cannot arise on this path.
